document: Stop Dartford Borough Council building anymore homes, Because of the amount of housing being built in the Dartford Borough the local hospital Darenth Valley can’t cope, the build up of traffic around Dartford bridge brings the whole area to a standstill still every day, people’s lives are being destroyed, the hospital is being bought to it knees, To improve people’s lives, to stop premature deaths

Fund free DNA ancestry tests for Transatlantic Slave Trade Descendants, The British government played a central role in the transatlantic slave trade.
Key aspects of its involvement:
1. Regulation of the Slave Trade
2. Economic Investment
3. Colonial Exploitation
4. Legal and Military Support
5. Resistance to Abolition, We think that offering free access to tests could restore cultural and ancestral identity that was forcibly erased during the centuries-long period of slavery. We think this erasure has left millions of descendants disconnected from their lineage, cultural heritage, and geographic origins in Africa.
 
Our key reasons for this policy include:
Reclaiming Lost History
Addressing Intergenerational Trauma
Cultural Empowerment
Correcting Historical Inequities

Require councils to keep streetlights on during the hours of darkness, Reports indicate that councils are turning off streetlights to cut electricity costs and save money. I think this is making streets less safe, increasing the risk of crime, and making it more dangerous for pedestrians and drivers. , Poor visibility at night creates hazards, and residents may no longer feel secure walking outside after dark.
 
I think street lighting is inadequate in many areas, which residents voice concerns about. Councils have spent significant amounts replacing lights with "energy-saving" bulbs, and I think turning them off defeats the purpose of these investments. I think that instead of cutting essential public safety measures, councils should find other ways to reduce costs.
 
I believe residents deserve well-lit streets for both safety and peace of mind.

Government to fund the creation of more arts, drama and music clubs, We think the government should give every child the opportunity to learn creative skills like music or acting for free, rather than families having to rely on private teachers. , We want children from families of all incomes to have the opportunity to discover their creative talent and for young people to have something fulfilling to do outside of school.

In many areas, community and arts centres for people of all ages are scarce. This can mean that kids resort to spending their time engaging in antisocial activities that effect our communities.
 
Every child deserves a place where they belong and can express themselves and it's unfair that in some regions, children miss out on these opportunities due to their parents not being able to afford private lessons.

Increase SEND funding for Early Years, We call for the Government to increase SEND funding for Early Years providers so they receive the same level of funding and support as primary schools. We have found in recent years that it has become increasingly difficult to obtain funding and support for the SEND children in early years settings., Early Years providers are expected to create and provide bespoke support plans to the individual needs of each child (often full time 1:1 care), sometimes at a financial loss for the setting. Early Years are expected to have everything the child needs, in place ready for school, ensuring the schools are in immediate receipt of any support and funding that we are denied.

Review, and simplify regulations about the operation of Large Goods Vehicles , The regulations about the operation of LGVs are multi layered and complex and have reached the point were, trainers and enforcers interpret the rules differently making it very difficult to comply. The Government should review and simplify them to ensure they are clear, concise and fit for purpose., The current regulations are a mix of domestic and EU law that evolved over time. An industry has grown up around compliance which we think flourishes because of  numerous 'grey' areas that exist in the governance of the operation of LGVs largely because the implications for operators who unwittingly get it wrong are so high.

Recognize Nowruz as a Cultural Celebration in the UK, We, the undersigned, call upon the UK government to officially recognize Nowruz, the Iranian New Year, as a cultural celebration in the UK calendar, alongside other cultural New Year celebrations such as Chinese New Year., Nowruz, a historic celebration, marks the Iranian New Year and the arrival of spring. It is observed by diverse communities, including Iranians in the UK. As a secular event, Nowruz fosters unity and cultural exchange. Recognizing Nowruz in the UK, as done in the US, would honor Iranian heritage and promote inclusivity and diversity. Recognizing Nowruz as a cultural celebration in the UK calendar would promote inclusion and encourage cultural harmony among communities.

Begin an enquiry into the PGMOL and all professional Premier League officials., Begin an enquiry into the Professional Game Match Officials Board, VAR operations and all professional Premier League officials., Fans are tired of the number of mistakes officials are making that ruin games and cost clubs millions.

Require daily sports in schools and increase school sports funding, We want the government to mandate daily physical education in schools, provide more funds for sports programs, and ensure trained teachers/coaches lead activities. , The funding could also help with the development of accessible facilities and create policies that integrate sports into the curriculum, making physical activity a non-negotiable part of education.
 
We think that daily sports at school is crucial for children’s physical and mental well-being. Regular exercise can boost endorphin levels and help to reduce stress, anxiety and depression—common issues for today's youth. Sports can improve focus, academic performance, and self-esteem while fostering social skills and teamwork. With mental health challenges on the rise, we think that incorporating daily fitness routines into school schedules could provide a proactive approach to supporting emotional resilience and overall well-being.

Apply the same energy efficiency legislation to all property - not just rentals, The UK government has announced plans to significantly increase energy efficiency standards for privately rented properties. Owner-occupied properties would not be required to meet the same requirements, which we think creates an unfair and illogical situation from an environmental standpoint., We urge the UK government to introduce a level playing field by applying the same energy efficiency standards to both privately rented and owner-occupied properties.
We believe that a fair and equitable approach to improving energy efficiency with the same standards is applied across the board. We think it is illogical from an environmental point of view to only apply the rules to the private rental sector.

Fund all secondary schools to have metal detectors, We urge the Government to provide funding for every secondary school to have metal detectors installed., With knife crime increasing, we believe metal detectors being installed in secondary schools would help reduce the number of school children carrying knives. Drastic action needs to be taken immediately!

Require all businesses to have environmental sustainability plans by 2030, I believe that all businesses should be legally required to have environmental sustainability plans to protect the environment as the quality of the environment is degrading., I also believe that this would also be a way to boost the economy as I think there is potential in this resulting in more jobs and businesses could save money, for example, on electricity costs by installing solar panels to their roofs.

Make it illegal for haulage companies to send HGVs into red weather warnings, I want the government to make it law that Heavy Goods Vehicles (HGV) are not allowed to be sent out into red weather warning zones., It could put the HGV driver and other members of the public at unnecessary risk.

Pause and review the smart meter rollout, I want the government to stop and review the rollout of smart meters. There is a possibility of the domestic customer losing their energy supply if there was an attack by malicious actors on the smart meter system., There is no definitive proof that a device that can communicate is more secure than a sealed device that cannot communicate. Therefore with the advent of artificial intelligence which bad actors can obtain I believe it is only a matter of time before the smart meter system is hijacked or disabled. New AI tools could make an attack like this more likely.

Ban AI companies from using music streaming to train AI, I would like the government to ban AI companies from training AI using music streaming. I think it's unfair to songwriters and that even if there were an 'opt-out' for their music, it would be difficult to contact every AI company to advise they didn't want it to be used for the AI learning., I fear some AI companies could employ tactics such as 'opt-out' forms that are overly complicated or don't work properly.
 
As a songwriter it can take decades to perfect your craft. It's difficult to get people to stream your music and make any money. One comfort is your songs are an original, unique statement of character, lasting long after your life. It's upsetting to think that AI could instantly consume the uniqueness and dilute it, creating similar songs.

Protect the 6 Nations Championship & Ensure Live Free to Air Broadcast, The 6N is a UK sporting icon, steeped in history & culture. We believe it fuels national pride, unites communities, inspires male and female youth and is crucial for social cohesion. We think maintaining free-to-air TV in the UK market would ensure equitable access, vital for a healthy nation., We urge the UK Culture Secretary to:
* Recognise the 6 Nations' national interest as a “crown jewel” sport
* Ensure live free-to-air access for all UK citizens
 
We believe live free-to-air 6 Nations access will:
* Promote social inclusion
* Support grassroots rugby
* Safeguard this iconic sporting event's cultural heritage

Require sports to be available on free to air tv, We urge the government to require all sports to be free to view and to think of the fans who can't afford pay per view TV., We believe all sports, especially Speedway and similar sports should be available on free to air TV. We think many sports including speedway are struggling as it is and could die out. We think sport needs to be seen by as big an audience as possible on main free view channels.

Make the Tour de France a Category A event so it is free-to-air, Make the Tour de France a Category A event to ensure it remains free-to-air in the UK., The Tour de France is the one of the world’s most-watched annual sporting event, inspiring some to take up cycling. We are concerned British cycling is already in decline, with the UK’s last UCI Continental team, Saint Piran, recently closing. We believe losing free coverage of this huge sporting event will worsen this, reducing visibility and participation in the UK. Cycling boosts health and sustainability—without free access, we think the next generation of British riders may never get inspired.

Recognise the production and serving of cask ale as Intangible Cultural Heritage, Following the UK’s ratification of UNESCO's Convention for the Safeguarding of Intangible Cultural Heritage, we call on the Government to recognise production and serving of traditional British cask ale as Intangible Cultural Heritage., Cask ale is unique to the UK – a historic and traditional production and serving method. We believe its flavour and texture is unrivalled anywhere in the world and can only be consumed in pubs with specific equipment and expertise. We think with the hospitality industry under financial pressure, it's vital we protect cask ale from further decline, both for its financial role in pubs, breweries, maltings and farms and for its cultural one in British society.

Hold an urgent Citizens’ Assembly on AI and enact its recommendations, I believe AI is being rapidly developed and released, without regulations to protect us from risks. Given the potentially profound implications, I think society must urgently be consulted through a national Citizens’ Assembly. The government must enact all recommendations, including on regulations., The government has said it wants to “unleash” AI, and mainline it into the country’s veins. But, Geoffrey Hinton, the Nobel Prize winner often called the ‘Godfather of AI,’ has warned there’s a 10% to 20% chance of AI leading to our extinction within 30 years.
 
I think the dangers of AI are enormous, with a possible loss of millions of jobs, that could upend society. I think citizens should decide how the technology is developed, by whom, for what purposes, the safety standards, and how to regulate AI and the tech industry.

Add animal care to the national curriculum , I think it would be a good idea to teach about animal care in secondary school because of people who would like to work with animals. , I think it would be good to know how to handle the animals in a calm way and know what to do at a young age. In my opinion, it's as important as learning to cook in food tech, or working with wood in DT.
 
I think it would be amazing to be able to see these animals, but it's not a case of, "oooh let's get some puppies in school to cuddle and pet!", but it's, " yes, let's handle some dogs and learn how to do it correctly!".
 
It could be something as simple as once every term going down to a donkey sanctuary, or visiting a dog kennel even! Just something easy to prepare for not only college, but a future job.

Put the dangers of methanol poisoning on the school curriculum, Young people are dying needlessly of methanol poisoning, most recently in Laos, Turkey and Vietnam. 

We think that children should be taught the dangers of consuming bootleg alcohol as part of the PSHE and/or Biology curriculum in school.,

Make St Swithin's Day a Bank Holiday, I feel St Swithin's Day takes us back to ancient core values of the British and the origins of paganism. An old saying is that this day's weather dictates the weather for 40 days after. More importantly, I think we need a Bank Holiday to break up the distance from Spring to end of Summer holidays., I think the Day is a significant piece of British cultural heritage, and making it a public holiday would help preserve this aspect of our national identity.
 
I believe in an era of rising climate awareness, a holiday celebrating our historic connection to weather patterns would promote eco-consciousness and our traditional relationship with nature.
 
I also think a new summer holiday could boost domestic tourism and create economic opportunities for the hospitality and entertainment sectors.

Require air-freighted produce to be labelled as such, Require produce to be labelled as air-freighted, integrating it with traffic-light nutrition labels and recycling symbols., There is no current legal requirement for air-freighted produce to be labelled as such. We think labels should provide details about how produce is transported, enabling consumers to make informed purchasing decisions. We believe by knowing the carbon footprint associated with produce, some shoppers could make environmentally conscious decisions, potentially reducing their overall carbon footprint. Air-freight is one of the most carbon-intensive transport methods and we think it is is potentially incompatible with Britain’s net zero commitments.

Stop Energy Companies charging more for day time usage when on Economy 7, We want the Government to stop energy companies charging higher rate charges for daytime electricity usage when customers are on Economy 7 tariffs. , Some pensioners are disadvantaged by having to pay more because they are home much of the day and we feel they are penalised for being tied to electric only heating systems.

Many retired people spend most of their time at home cooking, cleaning, watching tv, enjoying hobbies etc and, unless they do all this during the night, they are disadvantaged financially because their electric storage heaters consume their energy during the night at a cheaper rate. We think the daytime rate is unfairly higher than the norm and this is grossly unfair on people with limited incomes. We think the daytime rate should be reduced to the same as the standard daytime rate for fairness.

Review the curriculum to prioritise practical skills, The government should review the curriculum to prioritise practical skills like financial literacy, digital skills, and effective communication. We think this would replace outdated topics with real-world applications. Teach problem-solving, digital skills, and real-world applications., We think the entire education system needs a complete overhaul. Excessive testing must end, and the focus should shift to removing irrelevant topics that students find disengaging. In our view, some students barely grasp basic English, yet they are forced to study Shakespeare and what we see as needless topics like angles in polygons. AI is transforming how we access information, and we think the priority should be creating capable individuals ready for the real world—not mentally stressed kids forced to study irrelevant topics for hours each week.

Change the mathematics curriculum to be more relevant to real life, I would like the government to change the curriculum, so children can apply what they learn to their lives. I feel that currently, they are learning things that are not useful. I think children need to learn about real life maths e.g. mortgages, loans, debt and credit cards. , I strongly believe that the government should change the curriculum as it is not setting people up for life outside of school. I don't think children should learn things that aren’t going to help them in real life scenarios.

Extend the Victims Right to Review Scheme for Victims of Domestic Abuse, Formalise the VRR schemes in legislation and set out that victims of domestic abuse have a timeframe of 24 months to make an application., We think this would provide survivors with a crucial legal safeguard, empowering them to seek a review of police and CPS decisions within 2 years, ensuring that cases are thoroughly examined before dismissed. Domestic abuse cases are often complex, involving coercive control and psychological harm that may not be fully understood. We think this could ensure victims would have a greater chance of achieving justice.

Fund the building of 1500 artificial sports pitches by start of 2027, We want the Government to fund and build good quality football pitches for communities. , I believe that participation in sports like football is decreasing due to poor quality pitches. To combat this we should build artificial 3G and 4G pitches for football. which could be also for rugby. We think this could increase participation in sport.

New mansion square TRA want to have the right to choose our own energy provider, Allow residents to be able to choose fuel provider with affordable gas and electricity tariffs to suit vulnerable residents unlike vital energy has been providing. Vital energy are closed on weekends we also want a provider that is open 24/7 for emergencies especially for the old and vulnerable, To summons Peabody to allow us to be able to choose our own fuel provider for residents in New Mansion square Nine Elms to a provider that is open 24/7 for emergencies unlike the current provider that cost on average £60 per week for residents with a provider and tariff we are tied into and cannot change due to the terms of our tenancy agreement. Vital energy closes before 9pm also therefore residents have had no support in emergencies putting them at risk

Restore UK Leadership in Global Development – Reverse Aid Cuts, The UK is slashing development aid to fund defence—which we think undermines its global leadership & is risking lives. Aid helps fight poverty, prevent crises & boost security. Reverse ODA cuts & restore UK leadership in global development., We think the UK has long been a leader in global development, but that slashing aid from 0.5% to 0.3% of Gross National Income weakens our influence, risks lives, and undermines security. Aid can help prevent crises, foster stability, and support economic growth. We think cutting it is short-sighted and harms both the world and the UK. We call on the government to reverse ODA cuts and restore our leadership in global development.

Negotiate a minerals rights deal with Ukraine, We think the UK government must act decisively to secure a  mineral rights deal with Ukraine. We think this would boost economic growth, manufacturing, and energy security and reduce the deficit. We think a dedicated task force should negotiate the deal., We think the UK government must act to secure this deal, which could be worth billions, to boost economic growth, lower taxes, reduce the deficit, and strengthen key industries. We think it would ensure energy security, supply chain resilience, and global competitiveness, and could position Britain as a leader in manufacturing and AI-driven industry.

Require emergency service vehicles to use two-tone “nee nah” sirens., We feel there has been an increased use of American style “wailing” sirens on our emergency service vehicles. We think this is a mistake, and that these are less safe. We believe they also represent a loss of a small but important bit of cultural capital., A wailing siren's constantly changing pitch can disguise Doppler effects and interaural timing cues, which can make it difficult to discern the direction and distance.
 
We think a two-tone siren provides more predictable and consistent auditory cues that the brain can use for localisation.
 
Also, we want our emergency personnel to behave - and be treated like - British bobbies, not American cops. We view the siren an important subconscious nudge as to who we are and how we should behave.

Start funding and stop cutting resources for Youth services, More than half of young people want greater access to youth services in a bid to improve their mental health and sense of inclusion in their communities, new research from the NYA reveals. We think we need more funding and increased attention to the services for the youth and people of our future, One in 10 young people polled, from the youth agency survey's new research, said there are “no options at all” to access youth services in their area, while 66% said that there are “very few” or “some, but not enough”.
Youth services have seen a loss of £1bn of investment resulting in zero funding in some areas.
If crime is to decrease, we think this is the root of the cause you can help to reduce. We think providing a safe place for young people that can support mental health is important.

Get Southport pier reopened-a phased approach whilst full funding is secured, Back Sefton council, the leaseholders on Southport pier and the whole of this Victorian seaside resort, before its economy completely disappears . Southport and Liverpool Regions economy is suffering due to lack of footfall/interest in our town, a Victorian seaside resort with a closed down pier., Only sensible way forward we can see right now, in the immediate future, to get our pier open is to use the £3million that Sefton council already have for the initial pier re decking, to repair the steelwork that has been highlighted in the survey and redeck areas needed to make the pier safe to reopen whilst funds are still being sought for the complete refurbishment. The common sense approach and would give the town a much needed boost. Using the councils own figures 75% is safe to walk on!

End the "Special Relationship" with the USA, We call on the Government to end the Special Relationship with the USA following the USA’s approach towards Ukraine and Russia. , A strategic partnership between the UK and USA was heralded in 1946 when Churchill explained the necessity for a Special Relationship. Since then, this has included intelligence sharing, military co-operation and a joint approach to global crises, as well as a recognition of a set of common values focused on democratic governance and the rule of law.

Introduce a tax on AI usage & modify AI regulation to help UK jobs & workers, We call on the Government to introduce a tax on AI usage to fund worker retraining and require AI impact assessments. We want the Government to protect workers from large-scale automation that may result from AI., We are concerned that AI tools and advanced automation may be rapidly displacing human labour in multiple sectors. We believe that without Government intervention, we risk widespread job losses, wage depression, and social instability. We believe taxing AI usage can help fund retraining, while impact assessments can ensure responsible deployment. We believe that by doing this, the UK can preserve domestic jobs, protect vulnerable workers, and future proof our economy.

Ban fracking and drilling operations in coastal communities in England, We want the Government to stop plans for the appraisal of gas from coastal communities including the drilling operation, proppant squeeze. We are concerned it could damage the local environment. We think the Government should be prioritising green energy sources and not using residential areas., There are reports of communities affected, for example on the Yorkshire coast, who feel strongly about how drilling for oil could distress the local residents. We think it will damage tourism around the UK coastal communities which is how local economies on the coast thrive.

Ban councils charging council tax on secondary properties, We want the Government to stop Councils effectively doubling Council Tax for those who own holiday properties. , We feel it is undemocratic, arbitrary and unreasonable.

Preserve Shakespeare’s Legacy in Stratford Without Decolonisation, We urge the British government to ensure that William Shakespeare’s works and legacy in Stratford-upon-Avon remain free from efforts to "decolonise" them. Shakespeare’s plays are a cornerstone of British culture and a universal exploration of human nature, not a colonial artifact to be reframed., Recent trends suggest reinterpretations that impose modern ideological lenses, risking the erosion of their historical and artistic integrity. Stratford, as the heart of Shakespeare’s heritage, should remain a place where his works are celebrated as written, not altered to fit contemporary political narratives. This preserves their value for future generations and respects their global significance.  

We request that the government support institutions like the Royal Shakespeare Company and Stratford’s cultural bodies to maintain authentic presentations of his works, rejecting funding or policies that prioritise decolonisation over fidelity to the original texts. Shakespeare belongs to all humanity—let’s keep him untainted by division.

Ban realistic AI images claiming to depict politicians being published online., Ban realistic-looking AI generated images depicting politicians from being published online., There are realistic AI-generated images of politicians circulating on social media, often depicting them partaking in offensive activities. These are used by members of the public to criticise politicians they disagree with, however we think the realistic nature of these images could potentially mislead others into believing the images are real. We think this could potentially be used to interfere with elections, especially as the technology improves over time.

Add more life skills to the national curriculum for secondary education, We think schools fail to teach essential life skills. We urge the government to introduce mandatory financial literacy, survival skills and more mental health education (Years 7–9) and integrate apprenticeships into the curriculum (Years 10–13) to ensure students leave school prepared for life., We think many students leave without basic financial knowledge, survival skills, or work experience, leading to struggles in adulthood. We want students to gain real-world experience, financial literacy, and essential survival skills. We think this reform will reduce youth unemployment, improve independence, and create a stronger future generation.

Call for the UK to Withdraw from the 1951 Refugee Convention, We, the undersigned, call on the UK Government to withdraw from the 1951 Refugee Convention and its 1967 Protocol. We think the current asylum system is outdated and no longer fits the challenges our country faces today. , We think the increasing numbers of asylum seekers are placing immense pressure on the NHS housing, education, and other vital public services. We think British citizens are struggling to access basic services and affordable housing. We think it is time for the UK to regain full control of its borders and immigration policies to ensure a fair and sustainable future for all.

Fund campaign and incentives to prioritise British food and reduce food miles, We want the Government to encourage supermarkets to prioritise UK foods and reduce food miles. Measures could include incentives for local sourcing, clearer product labeling, and investments in sustainable supply chains, supporting local farmers and reducing environmental impact., We want the Government to act because we think prioritising British foods and reducing food miles will support local farmers, reduce carbon emissions, and promote sustainable agriculture. By incentivising supermarkets to source locally, we think we can lower environmental impact, strengthen the UK economy, and give consumers the power to make more eco-friendly choices. We believe this is a critical step toward creating a more sustainable food system, improving food security, and helping the UK move towards a greener future.

Review regulations on Battery Energy Storage Systems, Review the regulations on Battery Energy Storage System systems, including how close they can be built to homes, schools and hospitals, and rules around safety., These systems have a fire risk due to thermal runaway.
The fires can be self-sustaining and may last days.
Burning Battery's release hydrogen fluoride which can cause lung damage, severe burns and death.
There is an explosion risk from this type of battery
We think we need a minimum distance from the population, strict fire laws should be mandatory and all communities should be consulted.

Review the primary school curriculum to prepare children for secondary school, We urge the Government to review the national curriculum taught in primary schools to ensure Year 6 students are prepared for the transition to secondary school. , This includes exam preparation, introducing transition programs, providing teacher training, and improving communication between primary and secondary schools

Without proper primary education, children may struggle with the increased difficulty in Maths and English leading to them falling behind. Reviewing the primary national curriculum could ensure equal opportunities, addressing the achievement gap, for all children. As education evolves, the curriculum must adapt to prepare students for complex exams. Proper preparation reduces stress, fosters engagement, and supports long-term academic success and development.

Fund fire safety sessions to educate young people and prevent wildfires, We urge the Government to fund a programme of Fire Safety Engagement Sessions to educate youth on fire safety, prevention, and wildfire risks. We believe this can reduce fire-setting behaviour, protect the environment, and build positive relationships between the youth and fire services., Wildfires cause significant damage to ecosystems, homes, and cost taxpayers. In 2011, it was estimated that over 50% of these fires are started by young people, sometimes due to curiosity or thrill-seeking. We would like this programme, which will take place in high-risk areas, to involve collaboration with fire services, schools, and youth groups to educate young people on fire safety, wildfire risks, and prevention, helping reduce fire-setting behaviours.

End the Routine Use of Operation Brock on the M20: Use Only as a Last Resort, Operation Brock was designed to manage lorry queues heading to Dover and the Channel Tunnel, but it’s now used too often as a precaution. This causes traffic chaos, harms local communities, damages the environment, and wastes public money. It should be a last resort—not the default., We urge the government to end the routine use of Operation Brock on the M20 and use it only as a last resort in clearly defined emergencies. It causes disruption, pollution, and delays for local communities. Invest in sustainable freight alternatives, improve communication, and publish a full impact review.

Ban the sale and planting of the invasive plant: Spanish Bluebell + hybrids, I want the Spanish Bluebell plus it's hybrids to be listed as an invasive plant species and banned from sale in the UK. I also want a ban on the planting of it in gardens or in the wild., The Spanish Bluebell plus it's hybrid varieties is an invasive and quick propagator that is outcompeting our native English Bluebell in many areas. It is often impossible to eradicate from a garden and will quickly spread via air (seed) and underground (bulb) from one garden to the next. This can cause disputes as well as ruined gardens. It is readily available for sale online and in garden centres with no warnings about it's capacity to spread and carpet entire areas.

Eliminate VAT on hot takeaway food, We urge the Government to eliminate VAT on hot takeaway food., Many businesses, including fish and chip shops, are facing severe financial challenges due to the current economic climate. We believe these iconic businesses are vital to local communities and the UK’s cultural heritage. We think removing VAT could provide immediate relief, helping them survive rising costs and continue serving affordable meals to customers.

Reform curriculum to prioritise more outdoor learning/the outdoor environment, We urge the Government to prioritise more outdoor learning by making it a mandatory part of the national curriculum. We think more hours should be dedicated to learning in and about nature across all state schools in England to improve student wellbeing, engagement, and development., We think outdoor learning supports holistic development, boosting physical, mental, and emotional well-being. It nurtures key life skills such as teamwork, resilience, problem-solving, and care for the environment. Making it a mandatory part of the curriculum could ensure all children regardless of background, have equal access to these vital benefits.

Seek a No-Fly Zone over Central and Western Ukraine, We want the Government to work with international partners to support the implementation of a no-fly zone over central and western Ukraine. We believe this measure is urgently needed to protect civilians, humanitarian corridors, and critical infrastructure from aerial attacks., We think the UK can and should champion the creation of limited no-fly or humanitarian air protection zones in regions of Ukraine that are distant from active frontlines.
We believe seeking to implement a no-fly zone over central and western Ukraine could serve to protect vulnerable populations, maintain stability in humanitarian operations, and demonstrate the UK’s continued leadership in standing against unlawful aggression.

Dedicate funding for investment in Eco-Innovative Housing Projects, We call on the UK Government to invest in eco-innovative housing: sustainable communities with indoor gardens, clean energy, and nature integration. A portion of housing funds should support green estates that reduce emissions and restore the environment., Over £2 billion has been allocated to affordable housing, plus £800 million via the Affordable Homes Programme. However, none of these funds focus specifically on eco housing. We ask for a dedicated green housing fund, grants for sustainable designs, and support for developers creating eco estates with features like edible gardens, renewable energy, rainwater systems, and rewilding efforts. We believe this investment could help future-proof communities and contribute to climate resilience.

Protect Northern Ireland Veterans from Prosecutions, We think that the Government should not make any changes to legislation that would allow Northern Ireland Veterans to be prosecuted for doing their duty in combating terrorism as part of 'Operation Banner'. (1969-2007),

STOP A HOUSING DEVELOPMENT ON MOUNT BOVER LANE & MAIN ROAD, HOCKLEY, ESSEX. SS5, STOP HOUSING DEVELOPMEMENTS IN SMALL VILLAGES WITH 1 ACCESS ROAD, DESTROYING COMMUNITIES AND COUNTRY SIDE., WE NEED THE GOVERNMENT TO SCALE BACK ON RURAL & SEMI RURALHOUSING DEVELOPMENTS, IN HOCKLEY & HAWKWELL, WE CAN NOT COPE WITH MORE HOUSING , CARS AND PEOPLE. THIS WILL BRING A LOT POLUTION, CRIME, DESTROYING THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES, CREATING HUGE STRESS AMOUNGST THE LOCAL PEOPLE. WE ARE ALREADY BUILT UP TO THE MAXIMUM. THE SURROUNDING AREAS ARE BEING SUFFOCATED WITH HOUSING AND CARS.

Significantly strengthen and expand tax relief for the audio-visual sector, Raise tax relief rates for the UK audio-visual sector (with emphasis on animation and VFX) to match global competitors, broaden eligibility to include digital and immersive media, and introduce regional incentives to support growth outside of London., Though AVEC was a step forward from the existing Animation Tax Relief (ATR), other countries offer higher or more accessible tax reliefs (up to 40%) which draws talent and investment away from the UK. We believe that expanding relief will help retain world-class talent, attract international productions, support regional development, and bolster growth in the UK's creative sector.

Stop the Planning and Infrastructure Bill 2025 to Protect Nature, We think the Planning and Infrastructure Bill 2025 threatens irreplaceable habitats, weakens environmental protections, and ignores pressures on public services. We urge the Government to withdraw it to protect nature and our communities., We think the Planning and Infrastructure Bill 2025 would let developers destroy vital habitats by paying a levy, weakening protections for nature. Ancient ecosystems cannot be replaced. We think the Government should prioritise restoring empty homes, protecting green spaces, and investing in communities, not pushing through what we think is deregulated development that could harm people and the environment.

A statue of David Attenborough in the middle of Isleworth., David Attenborough has become the Grandfather the UK and the World has needed, including me., Sir David Attenborough has created a world that has become more aware of the wild and given us the opportunity to learn and grow with the understanding of nature.

Increase UK investment in renewable energy, I call on the Government to increase UK investment in renewable energy like wind energy, so we don't have to use fossil fuels and harm the environment., I want the Government to do this so that we don't have to rely on fossil fuels and cause harm to our environment. I think we can save our world if we do our part.

Review & modernise the GCSE curriculum to teach life skills & support students, We think the GCSE curriculum is outdated and ignores real-life skills. Many students also face tough home lives, like being young carers. We call on the government to review and modernise the system to be more relevant, inclusive, and supportive for all., We believe some students may experience depression and anxiety due to the GCSE system that we think is outdated. Some lack support at home, with parents who do not care or cannot provide guidance. We think the current curriculum doesn’t reflect the challenges we face. We think we need a modern, inclusive education system that prioritizes mental health, life skills, and support for all students to help us build a better future.

Increase funding for EHCPs to help address funding gaps in schools, We want EHCP funding to be increased for schools. For some, funding doesn’t cover the support required in the EHCP. We think that funding shouldn’t be based on banding but actual costs. EHCPs must fully fund staff, therapies, equipment, and training to meet a child’s needs effectively and lawfully., We believe funding doesn't effectively cover the full cost of supporting a SEND child. In some cases, minimum-wage learning support staff can exceed funding offered, this is without extra costs like therapies, training, equipment, and resources. Some schools are left struggling to meet legal obligations without adequate support. We believe increased EHCP funding is urgently needed to ensure proper care and inclusion.

Review Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill’s impact on non-school settings, Ensure the Bill does not require full-time non-school settings, including youth clubs, enrichment programmes, and religious or cultural centres, to adhere to the Independent School Standards if they are not providing full-time academic education in place of a school., We feel the Bill could unfairly classify youth clubs, enrichment groups, and cultural centres as schools, restricting their freedom to operate. We believe this would be an overreach that could limit educational diversity, harm community life, and goes against British values of freedom, diversity, and voluntary learning choices.

Provide funding for a nationwide, nature-rich river corridor network., Support farmers and landowners to make space for water with more, easily accessible funding schemes. We call on government to commit to providing financial incentives to help farmers create & maintain connected land along all river corridors (with buffers, wetlands, riparian tree planting) at scale., Many UK rivers are heavily altered from their natural state & can have difficulty handling our changing environment. This can have potentially disastrous consequences for people & nature. For rivers to provide us with essential benefits, we think they urgently need space to recover. Connected, natural areas of land along river corridors can offer this space, and could help to: restore rivers; improve water quality; offer flood/drought resilience; boost biodiversity and help safeguard food production.

Reintroduce the Help to Buy Equity Loan Scheme for First-Time Buyers, We urge the Government to reintroduce the Help to Buy equity loan scheme, offering first-time buyers up to 20% (or 40% in London) on new-build homes. We believe the scheme should be open to all eligible buyers and accepted by all developers., The Help to Buy equity loan scheme enabled hundreds of thousands of people to purchase a home. The new scheme, the First Homes scheme, offers up to 30–50% discounts but it has been reported that there has been slow uptake. We believe reintroducing Help to Buy could address this gap, support first-time buyers, and strengthen the housing market.

Fund support for Speedway, We ask the UK Government to fund support for speedway through funding targeted national grants and partnerships with local councils to help save clubs, improve infrastructure, and grow the sport., We are concerned that British speedway is declining fast. We are worried that clubs are closing, youth development is suffering, and that this historic sport risks extinction. We think public funding, investment, and national coordination is needed.

We must save the pre school for the kids and community, Increase Funding: Allocate more resources to early childhood education to ensure preschools can remain open and provide quality care.
*   Grant Subsidies: Offer subsidies specifically for preschools facing closure, helping them cover operational costs and stay afloat., Families struggle to find alternative childcar Preschools are vital community assets that provide essential early childhood education and care, laying the foundation for future academic success and social development. When preschools face closure, the impact extends far beyond the immediate loss of a learning environment. Families struggle to find alternative childcare, often disrupting work schedules and placing additional financial strain on households. Children may experience setbacks in their development, missing out on crucial opportunities to build social skills, cognitive abilities, and emotional resilience. Moreover, the closure of a preschool can have a ripple effect on the local economy, affecting jobs and reducing the availability of early childhood services for the community.
